features.text: Patient is 58 years old.
Patient reports trouble breathing more than usual, not previously experienced, occurring in different situations (outside and at home).
Shortness of breath has been occurring for a few months.
Shortness of breath does not have a specific time or trigger, but is more noticeable when outside or at home.
Patient does not have chest pain or a cough.
Patient experiences fatigue when shortness of breath occurs.
Patient had a chest X-ray and pulmonary function test, both of which were normal.
Patient has an inhaler that is used when symptoms occur.
Patient has not started any new medications.
Patient is not very active but tries to walk around the property.
Patient does not notice any swelling in legs or feet.
Vital signs are normal, pulse is okay, pulse ox is normal.
Patient does not appear to be in distress.
Lung examination shows faint expiratory wheezing bilaterally.
Patient does not have rash, swelling, or other issues.
Patient has not experienced dizziness, lightheadedness, or syncope.
Patient does not have nocturnal dyspnea or orthopnea.
Inhaler provides some relief but does not completely alleviate symptoms.
Wheezing is high-pitched, especially during exhalation.
Wheezing is not tied to a specific trigger, but is more noticeable when outside or at home.
Patient has not been evaluated for cardiac conditions such as heart failure, arrhythmias, or valvular disease.
Patient has not undergone cardiac testing such as an echocardiogram or ECG.
Patient has not experienced chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath with exertion or when lying flat.
Patient has not noticed any recent changes in environment that might be associated with symptoms.
Patient has not undergone recent blood tests such as CBC, CMP, or thyroid function tests.
Patient has not noticed any correlation between symptoms and specific times of day, seasons, or activities.
Patient has not undergone recent cardiac evaluations such as an echocardiogram or ECG.
